svg.text: [TRANSPORT] Internet reachability check (by IP address)

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: ✓ PASS

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: GeeNet reached the internet: 1.1.1.1 answered 2 of 2 pings in about 14

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: ms.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: [APP] DNS name resolution check

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: ✗ FAIL

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Your normal DNS server could not resolve names, but a public DNS

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: server (1.1.1.1) could. That points to the DNS server your computer is

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: using.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Technical detail: Configured resolvers: 192.168.1.1. Failed:

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: www.google.com(No such host is known); www.microsoft.com(No such host is

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: known). Public resolver 1.1.1.1 succeeded with 142.250.185.78.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Why we checked this:

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: GeeNet compares your configured resolver with a well-known public

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: resolver - if one works and the other does not, the fault is in the

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: resolver being used, not in the internet path.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: What this means:

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Your internet connection is fine, but the DNS server you are pointed

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: at is not answering properly. Names will fail to resolve for

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: websites and apps until the DNS setting is corrected.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Likely causes:

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: - The DNS server address is wrong, stale, or belongs to an old network

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: - The router is supposed to forward DNS but its DNS proxy is broken

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: - VPN or a security product took over DNS and is failing

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: - The configured DNS server is out of reach (blocked or offline)

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Recommended next step:

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: 1. Switch this computer to reliable public DNS (GeeNet can do it for

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: you)

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: 2. If a VPN is connected, disconnect it and re-test

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: 3. Re-test name resolution afterwards to confirm it is fixed

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Can GeeNet fix this?

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: This needs a repair that requires Administrator rights.
